records.literal_gloss: Why are nations in uproar, and peoples murmur emptiness?

en.L: Why are nations in an uproar, \q and peoples murmuring emptiness?
en.B: Why are the nations in an uproar, \q and the peoples muttering empty schemes?
en.R: Why are the nations so restless and angry? \q Why do people make plans that will come to nothing?

fr.L: Pourquoi [les] nations sont-elles en tumulte, \q et [les] peuples murmurent-ils le vide ?
fr.B: Pourquoi les nations s’agitent-elles, \q et les peuples marmonnent-ils des projets vains ?
fr.R: Pourquoi les nations sont-elles si agitées et en colère ? \q Pourquoi les peuples font-ils des plans qui n’aboutiront à rien ?

sw.L: Kwa nini mataifa yanafanya ghasia, \q na watu wananong'ona ubatili?
sw.B: Kwa nini mataifa yanafanya ghasia, \q na watu wananong'ona mipango isiyo na maana?
sw.R: Kwa nini mataifa hayatulii na yamejaa hasira? \q Kwa nini watu wanapanga mipango itakayoishia bure?

es.L: ¿Por qué están alborotadas [las] naciones, \q y [los] pueblos murmuran vaciedad?
es.B: ¿Por qué están en tumulto las naciones, \q y los pueblos traman planes vacíos?
es.R: ¿Por qué están tan inquietas y enojadas las naciones? \q ¿Por qué hace la gente planes que no llevarán a nada?

vi.L: Tại sao các dân tộc náo động, \q và các dân lẩm nhẩm điều hư không?
vi.B: Tại sao các dân tộc náo loạn, \q và các dân thì thầm những mưu kế rỗng tuếch?
vi.R: Tại sao các dân tộc xôn xao và giận dữ? \q Tại sao người ta bày ra những kế hoạch sẽ chẳng đi đến đâu?

ko.L: 어찌하여 민족들이 소란하며, \q 백성들이 헛된 것을 읊조리는가?
ko.B: 어찌하여 민족들이 술렁이며, \q 백성들은 헛된 일을 꾸미며 수군거리는가?
ko.R: 왜 민족들이 저렇게 들끓으며 화를 내는가? \q 왜 사람들은 아무 소용없는 계획을 세우는가?

decisions.choice: in an uproar: stirred up like a noisy crowd
decisions.reason: The verb (ragash) and the nouns related to it are used of a restless, noisy throng. The nations are stirred up and gathering, not only angry.

decisions.choice: murmuring emptiness: plotting what will come to nothing
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:2 of the person who murmurs the LORD's instruction (hagah). Here the peoples murmur "emptiness" (riq): plans with nothing in them, which will fail. The two psalms set the two kinds of murmuring side by side.

decisions.choice: Why are the nations in an uproar: prayed in Acts 4
decisions.reason: The believers in Jerusalem prayed verses 1-2 and saw them fulfilled when Herod, Pilate, the nations and the peoples of Israel gathered against Jesus (Acts 4:25-27).

decisions.choice: muttering empty schemes
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the sound of the verb, as at 1:2, and says what is empty (m2).

decisions.choice: "mataifa" for the nations and "watu" for the peoples, through the Psalms
decisions.reason: Hebrew pairs two words for nations and peoples in parallel lines. Swahili keeps the pair with "mataifa" and "watu"; "makabila" would suggest tribes within one country.

decisions.choice: "lẩm nhẩm" (L), the verb used at 1:2
decisions.reason: The Hebrew uses the same verb here as in 1:2, where the righteous person murmurs the LORD's instruction; Literal keeps the same Vietnamese word so the reader can hear the two kinds of murmuring side by side (see the meaning decision). Balanced and Readable say what the murmuring is: empty plans.

decisions.choice: "các dân tộc" for the nations and "các dân" for the peoples
decisions.reason: These are the two words for the world's peoples that run through the Psalms; each keeps one Vietnamese word, as the terms note sets for the whole book.

decisions.choice: "읊조리다" (murmur) at Literal, the verb used for the same Hebrew word in Psalm 1:2
decisions.reason: Literal keeps one Korean verb for the Hebrew verb so the reader hears the contrast with Psalm 1:2: the righteous murmur the LORD's teaching, the nations murmur emptiness. Balanced and Readable give the sense, plotting (meaning decision m2).

records.literal_gloss: Take their stand kings of earth, and rulers sit in council together against YHWH and against his anointed.

en.L: [The] kings of [the] earth take their stand, \q and rulers sit in council together \q against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed.
en.B: The kings of the earth take up their positions, \q and the rulers plot together \q against {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anointed king.
en.R: The kings of the earth get ready to oppose {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. \q Their rulers meet together to plot against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and against the king {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has anointed.

fr.L: [Les] rois de [la] terre prennent position, \q et [les] dignitaires siègent ensemble en conseil \q contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et contre {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} oint.
fr.B: Les rois de la terre se postent pour l’attaque, \q et les chefs complotent ensemble \q contre {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et contre le roi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a oint.
fr.R: Les rois de la terre se préparent à s’opposer {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}}. \q Leurs chefs se réunissent pour comploter contre {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} et contre le roi qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a choisi et oint.

sw.L: Wafalme wa dunia wanajipanga, \q na watawala wanakaa shauri pamoja \q dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na dhidi ya masihi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}}.
sw.B: Wafalme wa dunia wanashika nafasi zao, \q na watawala wanapanga njama pamoja \q dhidi ya {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na dhidi ya mfalme {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} aliyempaka mafuta.
sw.R: Wafalme wa dunia wanajiandaa kumpinga {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}. \q Watawala wao wanakutana ili kupanga njama dhidi {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} na dhidi ya mfalme aliyempaka mafuta.

es.L: Se apostan [los] reyes de [la] tierra, \q y [los] gobernantes se reúnen en consejo a una \q contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y contra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ungido.
es.B: Los reyes de la tierra toman posiciones, \q y los gobernantes conspiran juntos \q contra {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} y contra {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} rey ungido.
es.R: Los reyes de la tierra se preparan para oponerse {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. \q Sus gobernantes se reúnen para conspirar contra {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} y contra el rey que {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} ha ungido.

vi.L: Các vua trên đất đứng lên dàn trận, \q và các nhà cầm quyền cùng nhau hội nghị \q chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và chống lại người được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.B: Các vua trên đất dàn quân sẵn sàng, \q các nhà cầm quyền cùng nhau bày mưu \q chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và vị vua được xức dầu của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Các vua trên đất chuẩn bị chống lại {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}. \q Các nhà cầm quyền của chúng họp nhau bày mưu chống lại {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và chống lại vị vua {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đã xức dầu.

ko.L: 땅의 왕들이 나서며, \q 통치자들이 함께 모의한다, \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 그분의 기름 부음 받은 이를 거슬러.
ko.B: 땅의 왕들이 맞서려고 나서고, \q 통치자들이 함께 음모를 꾸민다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}와 그분의 기름 부음 받은 왕을 대적하려는 것이다.
ko.R: 땅의 왕들이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 맞서려고 준비한다. \q 그들의 통치자들이 함께 모여, 그분과 그분께서 기름 부어 세우신 왕을 거스를 음모를 꾸민다.

decisions.choice: take their stand: station themselves, ready to oppose
decisions.reason: The verb (yatsab, here reflexive) means to take up a position, often to face an enemy (1 Samuel 17:16; Jeremiah 46:4).

decisions.choice: sit in council together: plot together
decisions.reason: The verb is usually taken to be related to the word for a council or a secret plan (sod): they sit close and plan together, as in Psalm 31:14, "they plot together against me".

decisions.choice: his anointed: the king the LORD has anointed
decisions.reason: Israel's kings were set apart by being anointed with oil (1 Samuel 10:1; 16:13), and "the LORD's anointed" is a title for the king (1 Samuel 24:6). The word (mashiach) is the source of the title Messiah. The psalm speaks of the king on Zion (verse 6), the son of David whom God promised to treat as a son (2 Samuel 7:12-14). The New Testament applies the psalm to Jesus (Acts 4:25-27; 13:33; Hebrews 1:5).

decisions.choice: anointed king (B); the king he has anointed (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "king", because "anointed" is not a noun in ordinary speech. "Messiah" would bring in the later title at the cost of the psalm's own setting (m3). Literal keeps "his anointed".

decisions.choice: get ready to oppose
decisions.reason: Readable says what taking a stand against someone means (m1).

decisions.choice: "son oint" (Literal); "le roi qu'il a oint" (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The word means the king the LORD has anointed (m3). French keeps "oint" at Literal, the plain word for one anointed with oil, and explains it at the other levels as the English does; "Messie" would read a later title back into the psalm.

decisions.choice: "masihi wake" (his anointed) at Literal; "mfalme wake aliyempaka mafuta" (his king whom he anointed) at Balanced and Readable
decisions.reason: The anointed here is the king the LORD has anointed (m3). Literal keeps the one Hebrew word with "masihi", in small letters because it names the king's anointing, not yet a title; Balanced and Readable say who is meant, as the English does.

decisions.choice: ungido (L); rey ungido (B); el rey que él ha ungido (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew mashiach here is the king the LORD has anointed with oil. Spanish says "ungido", as the English says "anointed", and Balanced and Readable add "rey" as the English does. "Mesías" would name the later title before the psalm does.

decisions.choice: "người được xức dầu" (L); "vị vua được xức dầu" (B); "vị vua Ngài đã xức dầu" (R)
decisions.reason: The word names the king the LORD has anointed (see the meaning decision). "Đấng Mê-si-a" would turn the word into a title the psalm does not yet use; "người được xức dầu" says what happened to him, and Balanced and Readable add that he is the king, as the English does.

decisions.choice: YHWH is {{divine_name:주|야훼}} with the particle outside the span; there are no deity_pronoun spans, and God is "그분" with the honorific
decisions.reason: As the style guide (sections 7 and 7a) and the published Psalms 1 and 23: "주" by default, the name "야훼" as the alternative; "여호와" is not used. Hangul has no capital letters, so the deity pronoun setting has nothing to change; respect is carried by 그분, 께서 and -시-. This holds for Psalms 2-25.

decisions.choice: "기름 부음 받은 이" (L); "기름 부음 받은 왕" (B); "기름 부어 세우신 왕" (R)
decisions.reason: The anointed here is the king the LORD has anointed (meaning decision m3); Korean says the act of anointing in plain words, as the terms note does, and leaves the later Christian reading to the meaning notes rather than writing a title.

records.literal_gloss: Let us tear apart their bonds, and let us throw from us their cords.

en.L: "Let us tear apart {{deity_pronoun:their|Their}} bonds, \q and let us throw {{deity_pronoun:their|Their}} cords off us."
en.B: "Let us snap {{deity_pronoun:their|Their}} chains," they say, \q "and fling {{deity_pronoun:their|Their}} ropes off us."
en.R: They say, "Let us break free from {{deity_pronoun:their|Their}} control. \q Let us throw off the ropes {{deity_pronoun:they|They}} have tied on us."

fr.L: « Arrachons {{deity_pronoun:leurs|Leurs}} liens, \q et jetons loin de nous {{deity_pronoun:leurs|Leurs}} cordes. »
fr.B: « Faisons sauter {{deity_pronoun:leurs|Leurs}} chaînes, disent-ils, \q et rejetons loin de nous {{deity_pronoun:leurs|Leurs}} cordes ! »
fr.R: Ils disent : « Libérons-nous de {{deity_pronoun:leur|Leur}} pouvoir ! \q Débarrassons-nous des cordes qu’{{deity_pronoun:ils|Ils}} nous ont attachées. »

sw.L: "Na tuvikate vifungo {{deity_pronoun:vyao|Vyao}}, \q na tuzitupe kamba {{deity_pronoun:zao|Zao}} mbali nasi."
sw.R: Wanasema, "Tujiweke huru kutoka katika utawala {{deity_pronoun:wao|Wao}}. \q Tuzitupe kamba walizotufunga nazo."

es.L: «Rompamos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} ataduras, \q y arrojemos de nosotros {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} cuerdas».
es.B: «Hagamos pedazos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} cadenas —dicen—, \q y arrojemos lejos {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} sogas».
es.R: Ellos dicen: «Liberémonos de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} control. \q Quitémonos las sogas que nos han atado».

vi.L: "Chúng ta hãy bứt đứt xiềng xích của {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}}, \q và hãy quăng dây trói của {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}} khỏi chúng ta."
vi.B: Chúng nói: "Hãy bẻ gãy xiềng xích của {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}}, \q và quăng bỏ dây trói của {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}} khỏi mình."
vi.R: Chúng nói: "Chúng ta hãy thoát khỏi sự kiểm soát của {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}}. \q Hãy vứt bỏ những sợi dây {{deity_pronoun:họ|Họ}} đã trói chúng ta."

ko.L: "우리가 그들의 결박을 끊어 버리자. \q 그들의 줄을 우리에게서 던져 버리자."
ko.B: "그들의 사슬을 끊어 버리자," 하고 그들이 말한다. \q "그들의 밧줄을 우리에게서 벗어 던지자."
ko.R: 그들이 말한다. "그들의 지배에서 벗어나자. \q 그들이 우리에게 묶어 놓은 밧줄을 던져 버리자."

decisions.choice: bonds and cords: the straps of a yoke
decisions.reason: The words are used for the straps and cords that hold a yoke on an animal's neck (Jeremiah 5:5; 27:2). A yoke was a picture of a subject nation serving its overlord. The kings speak of the rule of the LORD and his king as a yoke to be thrown off.

decisions.choice: Let us: the kings and rulers speak
decisions.reason: The verse quotes the kings and rulers of verse 2 without introducing them; "their" means the LORD and his anointed king.

decisions.choice: they say
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the speakers, whom the Hebrew leaves the reader to see (m2).

decisions.choice: break free from their control; the ropes they have tied on us
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture of the yoke means (m1).

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}}
decisions.reason: "Their" here means the LORD and his king together; the English marks it with the deity pronoun setting, so the Spanish does too.

decisions.choice: "họ" for the LORD and his king in the rebels' mouth, with the deity_pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The kings speak with contempt, so they would not use a respectful word like "các Ngài". "họ" is the plain word for "they"; the setting gives it a capital as the English does, without making the rebels sound respectful.

decisions.choice: The rebels say "그들의" (their) of the LORD and his king, with no honorific
decisions.reason: These are the kings' own words (meaning decision m2), spoken in defiance; Korean would not give them a respectful pronoun for the one they are rebelling against. The English pronoun span has no Korean counterpart.

records.literal_gloss: [The one] sitting in the heavens laughs; [the] Lord mocks at them.

en.L: The one sitting in the heavens laughs; \q [the] Lord mocks them.
en.B: The one seated on the throne in the heavens laughs; \q the Lord ridicules them.
en.R: But God, who rules from {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} throne in heaven, laughs. \q The Lord makes fun of them.

fr.L: Celui qui est assis dans les cieux rit ; \q [le] Seigneur les raille.
fr.B: Celui qui trône dans les cieux éclate de rire ; \q le Seigneur les tourne en ridicule.
fr.R: Mais Dieu, qui règne sur {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} trône dans le ciel, se met à rire. \q Le Seigneur se moque d’eux.

sw.L: Yeye aketiye mbinguni anacheka; \q Bwana anawadhihaki.
sw.B: Yeye aliyeketi kwenye kiti cha enzi mbinguni anacheka; \q Bwana anawadharau.
sw.R: Lakini Mungu, anayetawala kutoka kiti {{deity_pronoun:chake|Chake}} cha enzi mbinguni, anacheka. \q Bwana anawafanyia mzaha.

es.L: El que está sentado en los cielos se ríe; \q [el] Señor se burla de ellos.
es.B: El que está sentado en el trono de los cielos se ríe; \q el Señor se mofa de ellos.
es.R: Pero Dios, que reina desde {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} trono en el cielo, se ríe. \q El Señor se burla de ellos.

vi.L: Đấng ngự trên các tầng trời cười; \q Chúa nhạo báng chúng.
vi.B: Đấng ngự trên ngai nơi các tầng trời bật cười; \q Chúa chế nhạo chúng.
vi.R: Nhưng Đức Chúa Trời, Đấng cai trị từ ngai {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} trên trời, bật cười. \q Chúa chế giễu chúng.

ko.L: 하늘에 앉아 계신 분께서 웃으신다. \q 주님께서 그들을 비웃으신다.
ko.B: 하늘 보좌에 앉아 계신 분께서 웃으시고, \q 주님께서 그들을 조롱하신다.
ko.R: 그러나 하늘 보좌에서 다스리시는 하나님께서 웃으신다. \q 주님께서 그들을 놀리신다.

decisions.choice: sitting: seated as king
decisions.reason: Said of God, to sit is to sit enthroned (Psalm 29:10). The kings "take their stand" on earth (verse 2); the LORD does not even rise from his throne.

decisions.choice: the Lord: the title, not the name
decisions.reason: This is the title "Lord" or "my Lord" ('adonay), used of God as master, not the name YHWH of verse 2.

decisions.choice: laughs, mocks: scorn for the rebels' plans
decisions.reason: God's laughter is not amusement but scorn: their plot is no threat to him (Psalm 37:13; 59:9). The psalm pictures God in human terms.

decisions.choice: on the throne (B); who rules from his throne (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what sitting means here (m1). Readable also names God and adds "But" for the contrast with verse 3.

decisions.choice: "Chúa" for the title Adonai, not "CHÚA" in capitals
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here has the title "Lord" (Adonai), not the name YHWH (see the meaning decision). "CHÚA" in capitals stands for the name, so the title is written "Chúa", as the English writes "Lord".

decisions.choice: "주님" for the title Adonai, with no span
alternatives: 주 (the default form of the divine name)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew here has the title "Lord", not the name (meaning decision m2). Korean writes the title as "주님" and keeps the name as {{divine_name:주|야훼}}, so the setting changes only the name.

source.text: אָ֤ז יְדַבֵּ֣ר אֵלֵ֣ימוֹ בְאַפּ֑וֹ וּֽבַחֲרוֹנ֥וֹ יְבַהֲלֵֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Then he speaks to them in his anger, and in his burning wrath he terrifies them.

en.L: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks to them in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, \q and in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning wrath {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} terrifies them.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks to them in anger \q and fills them with terror in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} blazing rage.
en.R: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} speaks to them in anger. \q His fierce anger makes them afraid.

fr.L: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur parle dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère, \q et dans {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} ardente fureur {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} les épouvante.
fr.B: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur parle avec colère \q et les remplit de terreur dans {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} fureur brûlante.
fr.R: Alors {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur parle avec colère. \q Sa grande colère les remplit de peur.

sw.L: Ndipo anasema nao katika hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, \q na katika ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} iwakayo anawatia hofu.
sw.B: Ndipo anasema nao kwa hasira \q na kuwajaza hofu kwa ghadhabu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inayowaka.
sw.R: Kisha anasema nao kwa hasira. \q Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} kali inawatia hofu.

es.L: Entonces les habla en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira, \q y en {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ardiente furor los aterroriza.
es.B: Entonces les habla con enojo \q y los llena de terror con {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} furia encendida.
es.R: Entonces les habla enojado. \q Su enojo terrible los llena de miedo.

vi.L: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} phán với chúng trong cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, \q và trong cơn thịnh nộ bừng cháy của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm chúng kinh hoàng.
vi.B: Bấy giờ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận phán với chúng \q và làm chúng kinh hãi bằng cơn thịnh nộ bừng bừng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Rồi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận phán với chúng. \q Cơn giận dữ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm chúng sợ hãi.

ko.L: 그때 그분께서 진노 가운데 그들에게 말씀하시고, \q 맹렬한 분노로 그들을 두렵게 하신다.
ko.B: 그때 그분께서 노하셔서 그들에게 말씀하시고, \q 불타는 진노로 그들을 공포에 떨게 하신다.
ko.R: 그때 그분께서 화를 내시며 그들에게 말씀하신다. \q 그분의 무서운 진노에 그들은 두려워 떤다.

decisions.choice: burning wrath: anger that blazes
decisions.reason: The word (charon) comes from a verb meaning to burn. Anger is pictured as heat, as again in 2:12, "his anger burns".

decisions.choice: Then he speaks: his words follow in verse 6
decisions.reason: Verse 6 gives the LORD's words. His answer to the kings is not a counterattack but a statement of what he has already done.

records.literal_gloss: And I, I have installed my king on Zion, [the] mountain of my holiness.

en.L: "But I, I have installed {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} king \q on Zion, [the] mountain of {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holiness."
en.B: "I am the one who has set {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} king in place \q on Zion, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain."
en.R: God says, "I have put {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own king in power \q on Zion, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} holy mountain."

fr.L: « Mais {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, j’ai établi {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} roi \q sur Sion, [la] montagne de {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} sainteté. »
fr.B: « C’est {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} qui ai mis en place {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} roi \q sur Sion, {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte. »
fr.R: Dieu déclare : « J’ai placé {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} propre roi au pouvoir \q sur Sion, {{deity_pronoun:ma|Ma}} montagne sainte. »

sw.L: "Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}}, nimemweka mfalme {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} \q juu ya Sayuni, mlima wa utakatifu {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}}."
sw.B: "Mimi ndiye niliyemweka mfalme {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mahali pake \q juu ya Sayuni, mlima {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mtakatifu."
sw.R: Mungu anasema, "Nimemweka mfalme {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mwenyewe atawale \q juu ya Sayuni, mlima {{deity_pronoun:wangu|Wangu}} mtakatifu."

es.L: «Pero yo, yo he establecido a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rey \q sobre Sion, [el] monte de {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} santidad».
es.B: «Yo soy quien ha puesto a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} rey en su lugar, \q en Sion, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo».
es.R: Dios dice: «He puesto en el poder a {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} propio rey \q en Sion, {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} monte santo».

vi.L: "Còn {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã lập vua của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q trên Si-ôn, núi của sự thánh khiết của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.B: "Chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là Đấng đã lập vua của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} \q trên Si-ôn, núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."
vi.R: Đức Chúa Trời phán: "Ta đã đặt vua của chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} lên cai trị \q trên Si-ôn, núi thánh của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}."

ko.L: "그러나 나, 내가 나의 왕을 세웠다, \q 나의 거룩함의 산 시온 위에."
ko.B: "나의 왕을 세운 이는 바로 나다. \q 나의 거룩한 산 시온에 그를 세웠다."
ko.R: 하나님께서 말씀하신다. "내가 직접 나의 왕을 세워 다스리게 했다. \q 나의 거룩한 산 시온에서 다스리게 했다."

decisions.choice: But I: the LORD's answer to the kings
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated for emphasis, and the "and" sets it against the kings: whatever they plan, it is the LORD who has made the king.

decisions.choice: installed: set in place as king
decisions.reason: The verb (nasak) usually means to pour out a drink offering; here, as in Proverbs 8:23, it is usually taken to mean "set up, install". Some connect it with pouring oil, the anointing of verse 2. Either way the sense is that the LORD has made him king.

decisions.choice: Zion, my holy mountain: the hill in Jerusalem where the LORD chose to dwell
decisions.reason: Zion was the hill of the city of David in Jerusalem (2 Samuel 5:7), later the site of the temple. It is holy because the LORD chose it as his dwelling (Psalm 132:13).

decisions.choice: God says
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker, as verse 5 implies (m1).

decisions.choice: deity pronoun spans only on free pronouns ("mimi", "wangu"), not on pronouns inside verbs
alternatives: a span wherever the English has one
decisions.reason: Swahili marks most pronouns inside the verb ("nimemweka", "I have set him"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so these psalms have fewer deity pronoun spans than the English. Free pronouns and possessives that refer to God take the span.

decisions.choice: "Ta" for God speaking, with the deity_pronoun setting in mid-sentence, and "phán" for his speech
decisions.reason: When God speaks of himself in a psalm he says "Ta", the word of one with authority, as the style guide sets; "phán" is the verb kept for God speaking.

decisions.choice: God speaks in 해라체 and calls himself "나"
decisions.reason: Terms note and style guide section 7a: God speaking uses 해라체 with 나, the voice of one with authority; an old royal word would sound archaic.

source.text: אֲסַפְּרָ֗ה אֶֽ֫ל חֹ֥ק יְֽהוָ֗ה אָמַ֘ר אֵלַ֥י בְּנִ֥י אַ֑תָּה אֲ֝נִ֗י הַיּ֥וֹם יְלִדְתִּֽיךָ׃

records.literal_gloss: I will recount concerning [the] decree: YHWH said to me, my son [are] you, I today have begotten you.

en.L: I will tell of the decree: \q {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "You [are] {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son; \q I today have begotten {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.
en.B: I will announce the decree. \q {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son. \q This is the day I have become {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} father.
en.R: I will tell what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has decided. \q He said to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, "You are {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} son. \q Starting today, I am {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} father.

fr.L: Je raconterai le décret : \q {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a dit : « Tu [es] {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils ; \q moi, aujourd’hui, je {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}ai engendré.
fr.B: J’annoncerai le décret. \q {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a dit : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils. \q C’est aujourd’hui que je suis devenu {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} père.
fr.R: Je vais dire ce que {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a décidé. \q Il {{deity_pronoun:m’|M’}}a dit : « Tu es {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} fils. \q À partir d’aujourd’hui, je suis {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} père.

sw.L: Nitasimulia habari ya amri: \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniambia, "Wewe [ni] mwanangu; \q mimi leo nimekuzaa.
sw.B: Nitatangaza amri. \q {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliniambia, "Wewe ni mwanangu. \q Leo hii nimekuwa baba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Nitasema kile ambacho {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} ameamua. \q Aliniambia, "Wewe ni mwanangu. \q Kuanzia leo, mimi ni baba {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.

es.L: Contaré acerca del decreto: \q {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dijo: «Mi hijo [eres] {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}; \q yo hoy {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} he engendrado.
es.B: Anunciaré el decreto. \q {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dijo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo. \q Hoy he llegado a ser {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} padre.
es.R: Contaré lo que {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} ha decidido. \q Él {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} dijo: «Tú eres {{deity_pronoun:mi|Mi}} hijo. \q Desde hoy, yo soy {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} padre.

vi.L: Tôi sẽ thuật lại sắc lệnh: \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với tôi: "Con là con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}; \q hôm nay chính {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã sinh ra {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.
vi.B: Tôi sẽ công bố sắc lệnh. \q {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã phán với tôi: "Con là con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Hôm nay {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} đã trở thành cha của {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.
vi.R: Tôi sẽ nói ra điều {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đã quyết định. \q Ngài phán với tôi: "Con là con của {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}. \q Từ hôm nay, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} là cha của {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.

ko.L: 내가 그 칙령에 대해 전하겠다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내게 말씀하셨다. "너는 나의 아들이다. \q 내가 오늘 너를 낳았다.
ko.B: 내가 그 칙령을 알리겠다. \q {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 내게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 아들이다. \q 오늘 내가 네 아버지가 되었다.
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 정하신 것을 내가 전하겠다. \q 그분께서 내게 말씀하셨다. "너는 내 아들이다. \q 오늘부터 내가 네 아버지다.

decisions.choice: I will tell: the king himself speaks
decisions.reason: In verses 7-9 the anointed king of verse 2 speaks and repeats what the LORD said to him. The psalm has four voices: the rebels (verse 3), the LORD (verse 6), the king (verses 7-9) and a closing warning (verses 10-12).

decisions.choice: the decree: the LORD said to me
alternatives: the LORD's decree: he said to me
decisions.reason: The divine name can be read with "the decree" ("the LORD's decree") or as the subject of "said". The sense is the same: the decree is what the LORD said.

decisions.choice: You are my son; today I have begotten you: the words that make the king God's son
decisions.reason: The LORD had promised David's son, "I will be a father to him, and he will be a son to me" (2 Samuel 7:14). On the day the king takes the throne the LORD declares him his son: "begotten" pictures a new relationship, not a physical birth. The New Testament hears these words fulfilled in Jesus: at his baptism (Matthew 3:17 echoes them), at his resurrection (Acts 13:33), and as the Son greater than the angels (Hebrews 1:5; 5:5).

decisions.choice: I have become your father (B); I am your father (R)
decisions.reason: "Begotten" is no longer everyday speech; Balanced and Readable say what it means (m3). Literal keeps "begotten".

decisions.choice: "son" lowercase; pronouns for the king follow the deity pronoun setting
decisions.reason: The psalm speaks of the king on Zion, and the New Testament applies these words to Jesus (m3), so pronouns for the king, like those for the LORD, can be capitalized with the deity pronoun setting (verses 3, 7-9, 12). "son" stays lowercase, as "my son" does in the quotation of Hosea at Matthew 2:15.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:tú|Tú}}, {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} for the king
decisions.reason: As in the English, the pronouns for the king who is called God's son follow the deity pronoun setting, so a reader who capitalises pronouns for God sees them capitalised here too. "Hijo" stays lowercase.

decisions.choice: the king says "tôi" with no setting span; God calls him "con", with the deity_pronoun setting
alternatives: "ta" for the king, with the setting
decisions.reason: The English lets the reader capitalise the king's pronouns, as the meaning decision explains. In Vietnamese the king would say "ta" only to his subjects, and it would blur his voice with God's "Ta" in the same verse, so he says the plain "tôi", which has no respectful capital form. God's word to him, "con" (my child), carries the setting instead.

decisions.choice: The king speaks of himself as "나" (내게) and God addresses him as "너", without honorifics
decisions.reason: The king tells what the LORD said to him (meaning decision m1). God speaks to the king as a father to a son, in 해라체; the English pronoun spans for the king have no Korean counterpart, since Korean has no capitals.

source.text: שְׁאַ֤ל מִמֶּ֗נִּי וְאֶתְּנָ֣ה ג֭וֹיִם נַחֲלָתֶ֑ךָ וַ֝אֲחֻזָּתְךָ֗ אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Ask from me, and I will give nations [as] your inheritance, and [as] your possession [the] ends of [the] earth.

en.L: Ask of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will give nations [as] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} inheritance, \q and [as] {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} possession [the] ends of [the] earth.
en.B: Ask {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the nations to inherit, \q and the farthest places of the earth to hold as {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} own.
en.R: Just ask, and I will give {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the nations. \q The whole earth, to its farthest edges, will belong to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.

fr.L: Demande-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je donnerai [les] nations [pour] {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} héritage, \q et [pour] {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} possession les extrémités de [la] terre.
fr.B: Demande-{{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}, et je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donnerai les nations en héritage, \q et les lieux les plus lointains de la terre comme {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} bien.
fr.R: Tu n’as qu’à demander, et je {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donnerai les nations. \q Toute la terre, jusqu’au bout du monde, {{deity_pronoun:t’|T’}}appartiendra.

sw.L: Niombe, na nitakupa mataifa [yawe] urithi {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, \q na miisho ya dunia [iwe] milki {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.B: Niombe, nitakupa mataifa uyarithi, \q na sehemu za mbali kabisa za dunia ziwe mali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.
sw.R: Omba tu, na nitakupa mataifa. \q Dunia yote, hadi miisho yake, itakuwa mali {{deity_pronoun:yako|Yako}}.

es.L: Pide de {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}}, y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré naciones [como] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} herencia, \q y [como] {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} posesión [los] confines de [la] tierra.
es.B: Pídeme, y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré las naciones como herencia, \q y los lugares más lejanos de la tierra para que sean {{deity_pronoun:tuyos|Tuyos}}.
es.R: Solo pídelo, y {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} daré las naciones. \q Toda la tierra, hasta sus últimos rincones, será {{deity_pronoun:tuya|Tuya}}.

vi.L: Hãy cầu xin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban các dân tộc [làm] cơ nghiệp của {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}, \q và các nơi tận cùng của đất [làm] sản nghiệp của {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.
vi.B: Hãy xin {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}}, {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban cho {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}} các dân tộc làm cơ nghiệp, \q và những nơi xa nhất trên đất làm của riêng {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.
vi.R: Con chỉ cần xin, và {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} sẽ ban các dân tộc cho {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}. \q Cả trái đất, đến tận cùng các bờ cõi, sẽ thuộc về {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}}.

ko.L: 내게 구하여라. 내가 민족들을 너의 유산으로 주고, \q 땅끝들을 너의 소유로 [주겠다].
ko.B: 내게 구하여라. 그러면 내가 민족들을 네 유산으로 주고, \q 땅의 가장 먼 곳까지 네 소유로 주겠다.
ko.R: 구하기만 하여라. 내가 민족들을 너에게 주겠다. \q 온 땅이 그 끝까지 다 네 것이 될 것이다.

decisions.choice: inheritance, possession: land held as one's own
decisions.reason: Inheritance (nachalah) and possession ('achuzzah) are words for the land God gave Israel's families to hold for good (Numbers 27:7; Genesis 17:8). The king is promised not one land but the nations, to the ends of the earth (compare Psalm 72:8).

decisions.choice: Ask: an invitation that is sure to be granted
decisions.reason: The LORD's words to his king continue from verse 7. The command to ask carries the promise: what the king asks, the LORD will give.

source.text: תְּ֭רֹעֵם בְּשֵׁ֣בֶט בַּרְזֶ֑ל כִּכְלִ֖י יוֹצֵ֣ר תְּנַפְּצֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: You will break them with a rod of iron; like a vessel of a potter you will shatter them.

en.L: You will break them with a rod of iron; \q like a potter's vessel {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} will shatter them."
en.B: You will crush them with an iron scepter \q and smash them to pieces like a clay pot."
en.R: You will break them with an iron rod. \q You will smash them to pieces like clay pots."

fr.L: Tu les briseras avec un bâton de fer ; \q comme un vase de potier, {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les feras voler en éclats. »
fr.B: Tu les écraseras avec un sceptre de fer \q et {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} les fracasseras comme un pot d’argile. »
fr.R: Tu les briseras avec une barre de fer. \q Tu les mettras en morceaux comme des pots d’argile. »

sw.L: Utawavunja kwa fimbo ya chuma; \q kama chombo cha mfinyanzi utawapondaponda."
sw.B: Utawaponda kwa fimbo ya enzi ya chuma \q na kuwavunja vipande vipande kama chungu cha udongo."
sw.R: Utawavunja kwa fimbo ya chuma. \q Utawapasua vipande vipande kama vyungu vya udongo."

es.L: Los quebrantarás con vara de hierro; \q como vasija de alfarero los harás pedazos».
es.B: Los aplastarás con un cetro de hierro \q y los harás añicos como a una olla de barro».
es.R: Los romperás con una vara de hierro. \q Los harás pedazos como a ollas de barro».

vi.L: Con sẽ đập vỡ chúng bằng cây gậy sắt; \q như bình của thợ gốm, {{deity_pronoun:con|Con}} sẽ đập tan chúng."
vi.B: Con sẽ nghiền nát chúng bằng cây vương trượng bằng sắt \q và đập chúng tan tành như chiếc bình đất."
vi.R: Con sẽ đập vỡ chúng bằng cây gậy sắt. \q Con sẽ đập chúng tan thành từng mảnh như những chiếc bình đất."

ko.L: 너는 철 막대기로 그들을 부수고, \q 토기장이의 그릇처럼 그들을 산산이 깨뜨릴 것이다."
ko.B: 너는 쇠 홀로 그들을 쳐부수고, \q 질그릇처럼 그들을 산산조각 낼 것이다."
ko.R: 너는 쇠막대기로 그들을 부술 것이다. \q 진흙 그릇을 깨뜨리듯 그들을 산산조각 낼 것이다."

decisions.choice: break: the Hebrew vowels; the Greek translation has "shepherd"
decisions.reason: The Hebrew letters can be read as "break" (ra'a') or, with other vowels, as "shepherd" (ra'ah). The vowels of the Hebrew text say "break", which fits the parallel "shatter". The ancient Greek translation read "you will shepherd them", and Revelation follows it (Revelation 2:27; 12:5; 19:15).

decisions.choice: rod of iron, potter's vessel: power that cannot be resisted
decisions.reason: The rod (shebet) is the king's scepter, the sign of his rule; made of iron, it cannot be broken. A clay pot smashed to pieces cannot be mended (Jeremiah 19:11). The picture is of the king's complete victory over the rebels.

decisions.choice: scepter
decisions.reason: Balanced says what the rod is (m2); Literal and Readable keep "rod".

source.text: וְ֭עַתָּה מְלָכִ֣ים הַשְׂכִּ֑ילוּ הִ֝וָּסְר֗וּ שֹׁ֣פְטֵי אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, kings, act wisely; be warned, judges of [the] earth.

en.L: And now, kings, act wisely; \q be instructed, judges of [the] earth.
en.B: So then, you kings, show good sense! \q Accept correction, you who rule the earth.
en.R: So now, you kings, be wise! \q Rulers of the earth, learn your lesson.

fr.L: Et maintenant, rois, soyez sages ; \q laissez-vous instruire, juges de [la] terre.
fr.B: Alors, vous les rois, faites preuve de bon sens ! \q Acceptez la leçon, vous qui gouvernez la terre.
fr.R: Maintenant, vous les rois, soyez sages ! \q Chefs de la terre, retenez la leçon.

sw.L: Na sasa, enyi wafalme, tendeni kwa busara; \q pokeeni mafundisho, enyi waamuzi wa dunia.
sw.B: Kwa hiyo, enyi wafalme, onyesheni akili! \q Kubalini kuonywa, ninyi mnaotawala dunia.
sw.R: Basi sasa, enyi wafalme, kuweni na hekima! \q Enyi watawala wa dunia, jifunzeni somo hili.

es.L: Y ahora, reyes, {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}} con sabiduría; \q {{plural_you:déjense|dejaos}} instruir, jueces de [la] tierra.
es.B: Así que, reyes, ¡{{plural_you:muestren|mostrad}} sensatez! \q {{plural_you:Acepten|Aceptad}} la corrección, {{plural_you:ustedes que gobiernan|vosotros que gobernáis}} la tierra.
es.R: Ahora, reyes, ¡{{plural_you:sean|sed}} sabios! \q Gobernantes de la tierra, {{plural_you:aprendan|aprended}} la lección.

vi.L: Vậy bây giờ, hỡi các vua, hãy hành động khôn ngoan; \q hãy nhận lời răn dạy, hỡi các quan xét của đất.
vi.B: Vậy, hỡi các vua, hãy tỏ ra khôn ngoan! \q Hỡi những người cai trị thế gian, hãy chấp nhận sự sửa dạy.
vi.R: Vậy bây giờ, hỡi các vua, hãy khôn ngoan! \q Hỡi những nhà cầm quyền trên đất, hãy học lấy bài học này.

ko.L: 그러므로 이제, 왕들아, 지혜롭게 행하여라. \q 땅의 재판관들아, 교훈을 받아라.
ko.B: 그러니 왕들아, 슬기롭게 처신하여라. \q 세상을 다스리는 자들아, 바로잡음을 받아들여라.
ko.R: 그러니 이제 왕들아, 지혜롭게 생각하여라. \q 세상의 통치자들아, 깨우침을 얻어라.

decisions.choice: And now: what follows from what the LORD has said
decisions.reason: "And now" turns from what has been said to what the hearers must do. The kings who plotted in verse 2 are now spoken to directly.

decisions.choice: be instructed, judges: accept correction, rulers
decisions.reason: The verb (yasar) means to be disciplined or corrected, as a child is. "Judges" here means rulers, who in the ancient world were also the judges of their people.

decisions.choice: you who rule (B); rulers (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "rule" and "rulers", because "judges" now suggests only courts (m2).

decisions.choice: {{plural_you:actúen|actuad}}
decisions.reason: The kings are addressed as a group. Spanish has two plural forms of "you": "ustedes", used in Latin America and the default here, and "vosotros", used in Spain, which the reader can choose.

records.literal_gloss: Serve YHWH with fear, and rejoice with trembling.

en.L: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in fear, \q and rejoice in trembling.
en.B: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} with awe, \q and let your joy be mixed with trembling.
en.R: Serve {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and show {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} deep respect. \q Be glad, but tremble before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

fr.L: Servez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dans la crainte, \q et soyez dans l’allégresse en tremblant.
fr.B: Servez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} avec un saint respect, \q et que votre joie soit mêlée de tremblement.
fr.R: Servez {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} et montrez-{{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} un profond respect. \q Soyez joyeux, mais tremblez devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Mtumikieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} katika hofu, \q na shangilieni katika kutetemeka.
sw.B: Mtumikieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} kwa unyenyekevu na heshima, \q na furaha yenu ichanganyike na kutetemeka.
sw.R: Mtumikieni {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} na kumheshimu sana. \q Furahini, lakini tetemekeni mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}.

es.L: {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} con temor, \q y {{plural_you:gócense|gozaos}} con temblor.
es.B: {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} con reverencia, \q y que {{plural_you:su alegría|vuestra alegría}} vaya unida al temblor.
es.R: {{plural_you:Sirvan|Servid}} {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}} y {{plural_you:muéstrenle|mostradle}} profundo respeto. \q {{plural_you:Alégrense|Alegraos}}, pero {{plural_you:tiemblen|temblad}} delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}.

vi.L: Hãy phụng sự {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} trong sự kính sợ, \q và hãy vui mừng trong sự run rẩy.
vi.B: Hãy phụng sự {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} với lòng kính sợ, \q và hãy vui mừng mà run sợ.
vi.R: Hãy phục vụ {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} và hết lòng tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. \q Hãy vui mừng, nhưng hãy run sợ trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}를 섬기며 그분을 깊이 존경하여라. \q 기뻐하되, 그분 앞에서 떨어라.

decisions.choice: serve: serve as subjects serve a king, and worship
decisions.reason: The verb ('abad) is used for a subject nation serving its overlord (2 Samuel 10:19) and for worship. The rebel kings are called to accept the LORD's rule.

decisions.choice: rejoice with trembling: joy and awe together
alternatives: with trembling kiss his feet (letters of verses 11-12 rearranged)
decisions.reason: The kings may rejoice under the LORD's rule, but with the awe that is due to him Some have proposed rearranging the letters of these words and the start of verse 12 to read "with trembling kiss his feet"; no manuscript has that text, and the text as it stands makes sense.

decisions.choice: awe
decisions.reason: Balanced says "awe" for the reverent fear owed to God; Literal keeps "fear".

decisions.choice: "phụng sự" (L, B); "phục vụ" (R)
decisions.reason: The verb is serving a king as his subjects do, and worshiping him (see the meaning decision). "phụng sự" carries both the service and the reverence; Readable uses the everyday "phục vụ" and spells out the respect in its next words.

source.text: נַשְּׁקוּ־בַ֡ר פֶּן־יֶאֱנַ֤ף׀וְתֹ֬אבְדוּ דֶ֗רֶךְ כִּֽי־יִבְעַ֣ר כִּמְעַ֣ט אַפּ֑וֹ אַ֝שְׁרֵ֗י כָּל־ח֥וֹסֵי בֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Kiss [the] son, lest he be angry and you perish [in the] way, for burns quickly his anger. How blessed [are] all who take refuge in him.

en.L: Kiss [the] son, lest {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} be angry and you perish [in the] way, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger burns quickly. \q How blessed [are] all who take refuge in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}!
en.B: Kiss the son, or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will be angry and you will come to ruin on your path, \q for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger can blaze up in an instant. \q How blessed are all who make {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} their refuge!
en.R: Bow before the son and honor {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, or {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will become angry and you will be destroyed along the way. \q His anger can blaze up in an instant. \q Life is truly good for all who run to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} for safety.

fr.L: Embrassez [le] fils, de peur qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} ne s’irrite et que vous ne périssiez [en] chemin, \q car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère s’enflamme vite. \q Ô bonheur de tous ceux qui se réfugient en {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} !
fr.B: Embrassez le fils, sinon {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mettra en colère et vous courrez à votre perte en chemin, \q car {{deity_pronoun:sa|Sa}} colère peut s’embraser en un instant. \q Quel bonheur pour tous ceux qui font de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} leur refuge !
fr.R: Inclinez-vous devant le fils et honorez-{{deity_pronoun:le|Le}}, sinon {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mettra en colère et vous serez détruits en chemin. \q Sa colère peut s’embraser en un instant. \q Ils ont une vie vraiment heureuse, tous ceux qui courent se mettre à l’abri auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.

sw.L: Mbusuni mwana, asije akakasirika, nanyi mkaangamia njiani, \q kwa maana hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} huwaka upesi. \q Heri [ni] ya wote wanaokimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}!
sw.B: Mbusuni mwana, la sivyo atakasirika, nanyi mtaangamia njiani mwenu, \q kwa maana hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inaweza kuwaka ghafla. \q Wana heri kweli wote wanaomfanya {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} kuwa kimbilio lao!
sw.R: Inameni mbele ya mwana na kumheshimu, la sivyo atakasirika, nanyi mtaangamia njiani. \q Hasira {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} inaweza kuwaka ghafla. \q Maisha ni mazuri kweli kwa wote wanaokimbilia {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}} ili kupata usalama.

es.L: {{plural_you:Besen|Besad}} [al] hijo, no sea que se enoje y {{plural_you:perezcan|perezcáis}} [en el] camino, \q porque se enciende pronto {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira. \q ¡Dichosos todos los que se refugian en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}!
es.B: {{plural_you:Besen|Besad}} al hijo, o se enojará y {{plural_you:irán|iréis}} a la ruina en el camino, \q porque {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ira puede encenderse en un instante. \q ¡Qué dichosos son todos los que hacen de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} su refugio!
es.R: {{plural_you:Inclínense|Inclinaos}} ante el hijo y {{plural_you:hónrenlo|honradlo}}, o se enojará y {{plural_you:serán destruidos|seréis destruidos}} en el camino. \q Su ira puede encenderse en un instante. \q Qué buena es la vida de todos los que corren hacia {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} para estar a salvo.

vi.L: Hãy hôn người con, kẻo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận và các người bị diệt vong [trên] đường, \q vì cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} bừng cháy nhanh chóng. \q Phước thay tất cả những ai nương náu nơi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}!
vi.B: Hãy hôn người con, kẻo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận và các người bị hủy diệt giữa đường, \q vì cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể bùng lên trong chốc lát. \q Phước hạnh thay tất cả những ai lấy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} làm nơi ẩn náu!
vi.R: Hãy cúi lạy người con và tôn kính {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, kẻo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nổi giận và các người bị tiêu diệt dọc đường. \q Cơn giận của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} có thể bùng lên trong chốc lát. \q Thật hạnh phúc cho tất cả những ai chạy đến với {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} để được an toàn.

ko.L: 아들에게 입 맞추어라. 그렇지 않으면 그분께서 노하시고 너희가 길에서 망할 것이다. \q 그분의 진노가 쉽게 불붙기 때문이다. \q 그분께 피하는 모든 사람은 얼마나 복된가!
ko.B: 그 아들에게 입을 맞추어라. 그렇지 않으면 그분께서 노하셔서 너희가 가는 길에서 망할 것이다. \q 그분의 진노는 순식간에 타오를 수 있기 때문이다. \q 그분을 피난처로 삼는 사람은 모두 얼마나 복된가!
ko.R: 그 아들 앞에 엎드려 그분을 높여라. 그렇지 않으면 그분께서 노하셔서 너희는 가는 길에 멸망할 것이다. \q 그분의 진노는 순식간에 타오를 수 있다. \q 안전을 찾아 그분께 달려가는 사람은 모두 참으로 행복하다.

decisions.choice: son: the Aramaic word for son
alternatives: take hold of instruction (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word (bar) is the usual Aramaic word for "son", used in Hebrew poetry in Proverbs 31:2, and the son of verse 7 is the natural one to be honored. Because verse 7 uses the Hebrew word for son, some read bar here as the Hebrew word for "pure": do homage sincerely. The ancient Greek translation has "take hold of instruction". The Hebrew letters are the same in each case; the question is how to read them.

decisions.choice: Kiss: an act of homage to a king
decisions.reason: A kiss was a sign of loyalty and submission to a ruler or a god (1 Samuel 10:1; 1 Kings 19:18). The rebel kings are told to submit.

decisions.choice: he, his, him: the son, or the LORD
decisions.reason: The nearest person is the son, and the son's anger is the LORD's own (verse 5). Taking refuge is said of the LORD throughout the Psalms (16:1; 25:20), so "him" at the end may point to the LORD; it may also be the son, through whom the LORD rules. The psalm does not pull the two apart.

decisions.choice: you perish in the way: you come to ruin on your way
decisions.reason: The words echo 1:6, "the way of the wicked will perish". With "How blessed", which opens Psalm 1, they tie the two psalms together as one introduction to the book. The phrase may mean perishing on the way, before reaching one's goal.

decisions.choice: quickly: in a moment
decisions.reason: The phrase (kim'at) can mean "soon" or "easily": his anger can blaze up at any moment.

decisions.choice: Bow before the son and honor him
decisions.reason: Readable says what the kiss meant (m2).

decisions.choice: Life is truly good for
decisions.reason: As at 1:1, Readable says what "blessed" means here.

decisions.choice: make him their refuge (B); run to him for safety (R)
decisions.reason: The verb (chasah) means to seek shelter; Literal keeps "take refuge".

decisions.choice: "Embrassez"
decisions.reason: The kiss is an act of homage to a king (m2). The old French verb "baiser" is vulgar in today's French, so Literal and Balanced say "embrasser"; Readable explains the gesture as the English does.

decisions.choice: se refugian en él (L); hacen de él su refugio (B); corren hacia él para estar a salvo (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew verb is seeking shelter, as under a shelter from a storm. Spanish keeps the picture of a refuge at Literal and Balanced and says it plainly at Readable, as the English does.

decisions.choice: "các người" for the kings spoken to
decisions.reason: "các ngươi" is archaic, and repeating "các vua" would be heavy; "các người" is how a speaker with authority addresses a group he is warning, as in the Gospels.

decisions.choice: "người con" for "the son", and "Ngài" for "he" and "him"
decisions.reason: "con" alone would read as "a child"; "người con" names the son the psalm has spoken of in verse 7. "Ngài" fits both the son and the LORD, so it keeps the Hebrew open as the meaning decision does.

decisions.choice: "그분" with the honorific for "he" and "him" in this verse
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves open whether he is the son or the LORD (meaning decision m3). Korean must choose a level of respect; the honorific fits either reading, so the ambiguity is kept, as the English keeps it.
